text:
sarah.arch: RFC follow-up — progressive model activation for on‑prem appliances. idea: ship a bundle that can start inference with a tiny "core" shard and then stream remaining model shards lazily. goal: lower outage windows for large model upgrades in low-bandwidth sites, start serving minimal SLAs during fetch. looking for thoughts on verifier boundaries, rollback semantics, and operator UX.
tom.core: sounds promising. how do we guarantee correctness while serving from a partial model?
priya.ops: +1. need to know what failure modes look like for operators — what telemetry and abort points we expose.
dmitri.storage: disk pressure is the main worry. if we keep partial shards around and the final model fails, we can fragment disk. eviction policy?
sarah.arch: good calls. design notes: 1) bundle = activation-manifest + core-shard + lazy-shard-index. core-shard contains an extremely small model (quantized tiny adapter or distilled skeleton) that can answer simple prompts. lazy-shard-index is a content-addressed list of shard blobs with checksums and signatures. 2) verifier verifies signatures for manifest + each lazy shard on fetch. 3) activation predicate is explicit: only promote to full traffic when N% of critical shards verified + local quality probe passes.
tom.core: can you paste a manifest example?
sarah.arch: sure:
```
activation_manifest: 
  version: "1"
  model_id: "redwood/llm-x-2026"
  core_shard: "sha256:aaa..."
  shards: 
    - id: 0
      hash: "sha256:bbb..."
      size: 12GB
    - id: 1
      hash: "sha256:ccc..."
      size: 12GB
  required_shards_for_promo: [0,1]
  signatures: 
    manifest: "kms-sig:..."
    shard_index: "kms-sig:..."
```

priya.ops: signatures per-shard ok but we shouldn't force verifier to download full shard before validating. lazy verify by fetching shard header (first N bytes) and verifying chunked checksums over the stream. that keeps HSM/KMS usage light.
dmitri.storage: eviction: propose two tiers. staged/retained. staged shards are in-progress and pinned until activation completes or is aborted. retained are older model artifacts kept for quick rollback but have TTL. eviction must consider a pinned budget.
tom.core: fallback model variants? if core_shard is too low quality, route to hosted fallback or slower full-model local path once all shards present. need API hook for runtime routing decision.
sarah.arch: agree. propose runtime exposes /model/health and /model/serve_mode (core|partial|full). operator/console can wire a routing policy: prefer local partial up to X qps, otherwise failover.
ops-bot: CI: https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/rlm-msdelta/342 — initial tests for shard streaming + verifier. status: flaky on 50mbps link emulation.
priya.ops: monitoring: important metrics: shard_fetch_rate, shard_verify_failures, staged_disk_bytes, promotion_time, quality_probe_score. add alert if promotion_time > configured SLO.
dmitri.storage: another tradeoff: content-addressed dedupe across models. saves bandwidth but complicates deletion when multiple model versions share shards. need reference counting in garbage collector and cross-tenant accounting.
tom.core: security: where does the verifier live? operator sidecar or kernel in operator plane? If verifier runs in the operator plane we keep trust central but risk exposing network path. If on-device, we need smaller verifier binary and periodic root-of-trust refresh.
sarah.arch: proposal: two-stage verifier. lightweight on-device verifier that checks manifest and incremental chunked sigs using a small PK bundle rotated by operator. heavy verification (full cryptographic audit) runs in control plane asynchronously for telemetry and signing policy. on-device verifier maintains a short-lived attestation token after a successful verify.
priya.ops: rollback semantics? if promotion fails after partial activation, we should have a reversible state machine: staged -> promoted -> active. abort from promoted -> revert: switch routing to core, mark promoted shards for cleanup, increment rollback counter, surface reason. rollback must preserve last-known-good metadata and optionally retain two-tier artifact set for fast re-promote.
dmitri.storage: operator UX: we need clear commands: `redwood-agent prefetch --manifest=...`, `redwood-agent promote --manifest=...`, `redwood-agent abort --manifest=...`. these should be idempotent and return machine-friendly error codes.
sarah.arch: long-term refactor idea: split activation policy into a declarative CRD so operators can author promotion rules (e.g., min-quality, min-shards, disk-budgets). sidecar implements the actuator. that moves logic out of binary flags into k8s-managed policies.
tom.core: compatibility: how do we handle older nodes that only understand monolithic bundles? need a migration: bundles include a "compat mode" header. server returns a lightweight fallback bundle (legacy) if node advertises old version.
priya.ops: testing plan: net emulation tests (10mbps/50ms), disk pressure, simulator for partial-verification failure patterns. also staged rollout: 5% canary -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback on quality regression.
sarah.arch: open questions: 1) exact signature scheme for chunked verification (deterministic vs streaming sigs) 2) retention TTL defaults and cross-customer dedupe policy 3) how to expose quality probes as canonical plugin interface.
dmitri.storage: +1 on pluginized quality probe. ops teams will want to inject domain-specific suites.
sarah.arch: action items: - priya: define alert thresholds and ops playbook for stuck promotions (due EOD next Wed) - tom: prototype chunked-header verification shim (PR draft OK) - dmitri: propose GC refcount schema and eviction policy doc - I'll draft CRD schema for activation policies and post updated RFC link.
priya.ops: ack. i'll start playbook skeleton.
tom.core: starting prototype tomorrow, will link PR shortly.
ops-bot: reminder: arch sync Friday 09:30 — add this RFC to the agenda.
sarah.arch: thanks all. if anyone wants to add edge cases (powercut during promotion, multi-tenant blob accounting) drop them here and I'll fold into the RFC.
